limitations: Mocked protocol execution does not establish rendering, codecs/devices, platform capture behavior, live streaming, or real OBS performance.
A finite watchdog expiration records that no bounded response was observed; it does not prove an indefinite hang.
The disconnect probe closes before applying an idempotent scene setter; it cannot establish behavior after an applied non-idempotent mutation.

result.instructions: Serveur MCP pour piloter OBS Studio sous Linux (scènes, sources, filtres, audio, streaming, PTZ, caméras) et ses plugins tiers documentés. 5 catégories d'outils : (1) domaine (obs_scenes, obs_config, obs_audio, obs_filters...) — à préférer pour les actions courantes ; leur description liste les valeurs valides du paramètre "action". (2) obs_ws_* (147 outils, protocole obs-websocket en miroir 1:1) — n'utiliser que pour ce qu'aucun outil domaine ne couvre déjà (les deux appellent la même API OBS ; ne pas dupliquer un appel domaine avec l'équivalent obs_ws_*). (3) plugin_* (66 outils) — plugins tiers documentés, toujours listés même si le plugin n'est pas installé sur cette machine (mcp_plugin_list donne le statut réel "active" ; appeler un outil plugin inactif renvoie une erreur explicite, pas un échec silencieux). (4) mcp_* (14 outils) — introspection serveur, recherche/lecture de la documentation locale (mcp_doc_search, mcp_doc_get), gestion des plugins (install/uninstall/update), config. (5) obs_linux_* (5 outils) — raccourcis de création pour les sources Linux courantes (V4L2, PipeWire, PulseAudio). Pour le schéma exact d'un outil précis : mcp_get_tool_schema. Pour un détail non couvert par une description (champs exacts d'une requête obs-websocket, README amont d'un plugin) : mcp_doc_search puis mcp_doc_get.

Deinterlace mode values (inputDeinterlaceMode): OBS_DEINTERLACE_MODE_DISABLE/DISCARD/RETRO/BLEND/BLEND_2X/LINEAR/LINEAR_2X/YADIF/YADIF_2X; field order (inputDeinterlaceFieldOrder): OBS_DEINTERLACE_FIELD_ORDER_TOP/BOTTOM. tools.name: obs_scene_items
tools.description: Scene item transform and stacking order (front/back) — actions: list, create, remove, set_transform, get_index, set_index, move_up, move_down, move_to_top, move_to_bottom, reset_transform, fit_to_screen, stretch_to_screen, rotate_90_cw, rotate_90_ccw, rotate_180, flip_horizontal, flip_vertical, center_to_screen, center_horizontal, center_vertical (sceneName always required, never implicit). Mirrors OBS's right-click "Ordonner" (stacking order) and "Transformer" (transform) menus. Stacking order: a higher sceneItemIndex is drawn later, i.e. more toward the front/visible; index 0 is the back-most layer — move_to_top brings a source fully in front (e.g. a webcam hidden behind a capture card), move_to_bottom sends it fully behind. reset_transform/fit_to_screen/stretch_to_screen exactly reproduce OBS's own frontend logic (position/scale/bounds fully overwritten, no ambiguity). rotate_90_cw/rotate_90_ccw/rotate_180/flip_horizontal/flip_vertical set the rotation/scale field directly but — unlike OBS's UI — do NOT also reposition the item to keep its visible corner anchored; follow up with center_to_screen/set_transform if the resulting position looks off. center_to_screen/center_horizontal/center_vertical are accurate for the common case (no crop, rotation a multiple of 90°) but do not replicate OBS's full crop-aware transform matrix. NOTE: per-source "Transition à l'affichage"/"Transition de masquage" (show/hide transition) has NO obs-websocket equivalent at all (verified against source) — not reachable through this server. CONVENTIONS (defaults — an explicit user instruction about position, size, layering, or intentional overflow ALWAYS takes priority over these): 1) Keep every item fully inside the canvas (GetVideoSettings' baseWidth/baseHeight) when creating/positioning/resizing via create/set_transform/fit_to_screen — never let position+bounds/scale push a corner past the canvas edges; verify with list or a screenshot after the change. 2) A camera-type source (webcam, capture card used as a face/PIP cam) should generally be brought to the front (move_to_top) so it stays visible, unless the user asks for it to be behind something. (domaine — param action requis)

Unlike obs_screenshot (one-shot), each source is a persistent named config (source_name, cadence_ms, image_format, image_width, image_height, quality) that a background worker captures on its own schedule, keeping only the most recent 10 images.
